decision.title: QQQ ETF vs Certificate of Deposit
decision.description: Deciding between investing in the QQQ ETF (tracking the Nasdaq-100) and placing money in a Certificate of Deposit (CD) involves weighing growth potential, risk, liquidity, and time horizon. This comparison focuses on qualitative factors that affect the long‑term suitability of each option.
decision.originalInput: Should I invest in QQQ ETF or Certificate of Deposit?

tags.name: Risk tolerance
tags.description: How much volatility can you comfortably endure?

targets.consideration: Are you comfortable with the possibility of short‑term losses in exchange for higher long‑term growth?
Do you prefer a guaranteed return with minimal risk to your principal?

tags.name: Investment horizon
tags.description: When will you need the invested funds?

targets.consideration: If you won’t need the money for at least 5–10 years, does the QQQ’s growth potential align with your timeline?
If you need the money within a few years, does a CD’s fixed term match your liquidity needs?

tags.name: Liquidity requirement
tags.description: How easily do you need to access your money?

targets.consideration: Can you tolerate selling ETF shares at any time, knowing the price may fluctuate?
Are you willing to accept early‑withdrawal penalties if you need the money before the CD matures?

tags.name: Inflation protection
tags.description: Will the investment keep pace with rising prices?

targets.consideration: Does the QQQ’s historical growth suggest it could outpace inflation over the long term?
Does the CD’s fixed interest rate likely exceed inflation, or could it lose purchasing power?
